text.p: Nocopi Technologies Inc said on Monday it had renegotiated its agreement with Georgia-Pacific Corp on check-clearing technology.

The company said in a statement that Georgia-Pacific would maintain the exclusive right to incorporate Nocopi technology in paper sold for personal and commercial checks to its four major check customers. Nocopi will reacquire the ability to sell its technology directly to all other U.S. check printers.

The statement said the changes arose from "a technical development at Nocopi which has opened up the potential for an alternative method of applying the Nocopi technology to checks and other security documents, and the slower-than-anticipated revenue growth from Georgia-Pacific which, combined with delays in the development of other areas of Nocopi's business" has harmed Nocopi's third- and fourth- quarter projections.

The new agreement "will have a short-term effect on Nocopi's revenues," the statement said. "Over the longer term, Nocopi expects that an increased royalty rate from Georgia-Pacific combined with a more open market segment ... will help surpass the previously guaranteed revenue from Georgia-Pacific."
